Game Rules

Nineball (9-Ball) Pool Rules & Mechanics

Nineball (9-ball) is a rotation pool game played with nine object balls numbered 1 through 9 and a cue ball. On every shot, the cue ball must contact the lowest-numbered ball on the table first, but balls do not need to be pocketed in numerical order.

  • The Opening Break: The 1-ball is placed at the apex of the diamond rack, and the 9-ball is placed in the center.
  • Legal Contact: Failing to strike the lowest-numbered ball first results in a foul, granting your opponent ball-in-hand anywhere on the table.
  • Winning Condition: The player who legally pockets the 9-ball at any point during the frame wins the game.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Is this 9-ball pool game free to play?

    Yes, it is 100% free and open-source. You can play directly in any modern browser on PC, Mac, Linux, Android, or iOS with no fees, ads, or subscriptions.

  • Do I need to install software or register an account?

    No registration or download is needed. Click the play button to immediately load the 3D WebGL table and start playing single-player practice, playing against AI bots, or joining multiplayer games in the lobby.

  • How do 9-ball pool rules work in this simulator?

    9-ball is a rotation pool game. On every shot, the cue ball must contact the lowest-numbered ball remaining on the table first. The player who legally pockets the 9-ball wins the game.
